ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $D$ is a point on side $BC$, and $AB=AD=DC$. If $AC=BC$, what is the degree measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $ \angle C=x$\\
Since $AD=DC$\\
Then $\angle DAC=\angle C=x$\\
Thus $\angle ADB=2x$\\
Since $AB=AD$\\
Then $\angle B=\angle ADB=2x$\\
Since $AC=BC$\\
Then $\angle BAC=\angle B=2x$\\
In $ \triangle ABC$,\\
$2x+2x+x=180^\circ$\\
Therefore $x=36^\circ$\\
Thus, the measure of $\angle C$ is $\boxed{36^\circ}$

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $D$ is a point on side $BC$, and $AB=AD=DC$. If $AC=BC$, what is the degree measure of $\angle C$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle C=x$\\
Since $AD=DC$\\
Then $\angle DAC=\angle C=x$\\
Thus $\angle ADB=2x$\\
Since $AB=AD$\\
Then $\angle B=\angle ADB=2x$\\
Since $AC=BC$\\
Then $\angle BAC=\angle B=2x$\\
In $\triangle ABC$,\\
$2x+2x+x=180^\circ$\\
Therefore $x=36^\circ$\\
Thus, the measure of $\angle C$ is $\boxed{36^\circ}$

The problem gives AB=AD=DC, and AC=BC. Reasoning: According to the specified method, because AC=BC, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle with C as the vertex, so the base angles ∠A=∠B. Let ∠A=∠B=y, then ∠C=180°-2y. Because D is on BC, ray BD is collinear with BC, ∠ABD=∠ABC=y. In triangle ABD, AB=AD, so the base angles ∠ABD=∠BDA=y, therefore ∠BAD=180°-2y. In triangle ADC, AD=DC, so ∠DAC=∠ACD. Also because C, D, B are collinear, ∠ACD is the outer triangle's ∠ACB, namely ∠C=180°-2y, so ∠DAC=180°-2y. AD divides ∠A into ∠BAD and ∠DAC, therefore y=∠A=∠BAD+∠DAC=(180°-2y)+(180°-2y). Solving gives y=360°-4y, 5y=360°, y=72°. Therefore ∠C=180°-2y=180°-144°=36°.
